soc.t: Modernising threat hunting: Using Semantic Search to Find Risky AI Agent Behavior
soc.x: I tested vector search on 7,454 turns of my own agent sessions. One in seven sessions needed review, the agent’s reasoning carried more signal than the prompt, and the stored vectors answer questions nobody thought to ask at ingest.

soc.t: When trust becomes the payload: Inside the threats, etc quarterly report

soc.t: Gangsters, Money Trails, and Wuffy | Huntress
soc.x: A $30 AI toy dog led Mastercard to 250+ scam sites. See how small charges and ransomware payouts follow the same money trail, and how to cut it off.

soc.t: Kernel eviction notice: What wesp.sys reveals about the Windows Endpoint Security Platform
soc.x: Microsoft wants EDR out of the Windows kernel, and the preview binaries show wesp.sys telling a user-mode client that a process is starting, with nothing in its imports to let that client block it.

soc.t: How CVE-2026-73570 turns a Zimbra log file into remote code execution
soc.x: We reproduced the Zimbra command injection vulnerability and found that several public PoCs write a payload Swatchdog never matches, so a failed test looks like a patched server.

soc.t: php2shell: Assessing Elastic detection coverage relevant to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
soc.x: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are critical PHP core RCE flaws that leaked ahead of disclosure. We cover what is verified, why exploitation converges on a web server spawning a shell, and the Elastic detections developed to catch this behavior.
